content: Northumbria University is a contemporary higher education institution situated in Newcastle upon Tyne, in the North East of England. The university offers approximately 500 academic programs across nine distinct schools: Applied Sciences; Arts and Social Sciences; Built Environment; Design; Health, Community, and Education; Computing, Engineering, and Information Sciences; Law; Newcastle Business School; and Psychology and Sports Sciences. The university operates two campuses. The primary campus, known as the City Campus, is located in the heart of Newcastle upon Tyne. The secondary campus, referred to as the Coach Lane Campus, is situated a few miles outside the city. The Coach Lane Campus exclusively houses the School of Health, Community, and Education Studies, while all other schools are based at the City Campus. A free shuttle bus service is available to facilitate transportation between the two campuses. Northumbria University is currently undergoing a £100 million development project aimed at enhancing and expanding its City Campus. This includes the creation of a state-of-the-art, seven-acre site called City Campus East, adjacent to the main campus. This new site will accommodate the Schools of Law, Design, and Newcastle Business School. Additionally, improvements to City Campus West are underway, including the construction of a new footbridge connecting the East and West Campuses across the central motorway, as well as pedestrianization and the incorporation of green spaces into the teaching environment. The first phase of this expansion is expected to be completed by September 2007. However, the project faced a setback on April 9, 2007, when a building intended for student accommodations was destroyed by fire. The nearby School of Design sustained minor heat damage before the fire was brought under control. The origins of Northumbria University can be traced back to three regional colleges: Rutherford College of Technology, the College of Art & Industrial Design, and the Municipal College of Commerce. These institutions merged to form Newcastle Polytechnic in 1969, which became a major regional center for teacher training following the incorporation of the City College of Education in 1974 and the Northern Counties College of Education in 1976. Northumbria was officially established as a university in 1992 under the name University of Northumbria at Newcastle. The name was later simplified to Northumbria University in 2002. Notable alumni of Northumbria University include Sting, the renowned English musician; Tunde Baiyewu, lead vocalist of the Lighthouse Family; Steve Cram, an English athlete and television presenter; Scott Henshall, a fashion designer; Jonathan Ive, the industrial designer behind the iMac and iPod; Alexei Mordashov, a Russian business oligarch; Neil Marshall, a film director; Paul Copley, an actor; Toby Flood, an England rugby international and Newcastle Falcons player; and Martin Corry, an England rugby international and Leicester Tigers player. The Students' Union at Northumbria University represents all students enrolled at the institution. It organizes a variety of student activities and provides several venues for socializing in a safe environment, including Bar One and Reds. The Union hosts various club nights, such as the bi-weekly Rattled by the Rush, which features indie music, and Get Y' Skates On, catering to alternative music enthusiasts. The Union also publishes a monthly student newspaper called Northumbria Student, which includes the popular entertainment section Poly Scene.
